displayName: Wright for Git: Multi-Repo Log, Commit & Shelf
description: IntelliJ-style Git tool windows for multi-repository workspaces: a log with commit graph, branches tree and powerful filters, a Commit window with changelists and partial commits, a cross-repository Shelf, interactive rebase and merge conflict resolution.
capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces: Wright runs git in the workspace's repositories, and a repository's Git configuration and hooks can execute arbitrary commands, so it needs a trusted workspace.
container.title: Git
config.defaultFavoriteBranches: Branches marked as favorites in a workspace until you star or unstar any branch there (local and remote branches with these names, e.g. `main`, `origin/main`). Set to `[]` to start with no favorites.
config.maxCommits: Maximum number of commits loaded into the log (total across all repositories).
config.autoRefresh: Refresh the log automatically when branches, tags or HEAD change.
config.scanDepth: How many folder levels below each workspace folder are scanned for Git repositories (0 = only the workspace folder itself).
config.scanExclude: Folder names skipped when scanning for repositories.
command.openSelectedFile: Open Selected File in Changed Files
command.selectInSelectedFile: Select In… for Selected File in Changed Files
config.language: Language of the Wright panel, dialogs and messages. Command names and settings always follow the VS Code display language.
config.language.auto: Follow the VS Code display language
config.issueLinks: Turn issue references in commit messages into links. Each rule has a regular expression `pattern` and a `url` that can use `$0`, `$1`… and `{repo}` (the web URL of `origin`). Example: `{ "pattern": "PROJ-\\d+", "url": "https://jira.example.com/browse/$0" }`. When empty, `#123` links to the issue on GitHub / GitLab.
config.issueLinks.url: Link URL; $0 is the whole match, $1… are groups, {repo} is the web URL of origin
